samples.text: In the meantime, valuation for the period runs on a manual basis: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. The override exists because the confirmed cause sits in reference data, recorded as stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register, and a correction to the register itself needs more time than the period allows. Compared with the normal automated run, this route is slower and depends on the accuracy of each manual entry. Its output stays provisional until the register is corrected and the overridden mapping is checked against it. The override keeps the period moving and leaves the stale mapping in the register, so a run after this period can fail the same way unless the mapping is corrected first. Teams that can wait for the corrected register need to wait for it. Teams on a close deadline can use the overridden figures, marked as provisional, and plan for a reconciliation once the register is fixed. Nobody needs to rebuild their own

The inventory valuation service failed because its agency code mapping was out of date, and the confirmed cause is recorded as stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Legacy and cloud agency codes are both in use and are not interchangeable, so the valuation depends on that mapping being current for every record it reads. An earlier explanation was recorded first and later withdrawn. On the morning of the failure, the incident team logged the cause as overnight ERP outage, and the first checks followed that line. Direct evidence ruled it out a little over two hours later: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the upstream source cleared, the team turned to the reference data and confirmed the stale entry early that afternoon. Two days on, the review classified the underlying problem as a control gap, recorded as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer.
